problem:
Mark jogs every day in the neighborhood park. Last week he ran the following distances, in kilometers:

$$
1\,\text{km},\,3\,\text{km},\,2\,\text{km},\,3\,\text{km},\,1\,\text{km},\,1\,\text{km},\,3\,\text{km}
$$

What is the mean distance Mark jogged last week?

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Mean of a Data Set
examples.problem:
What is the mean of the following data set?

$$
9, \: 10, \: 8, \: 11, \: 12
$$
examples.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the mean is denoted by $\overline{x}$ and is given by the following formula:

$$
\overline{x} = \dfrac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n x_i
$$

Here, there are $n=5$ data points. Adding up all the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i} & =9+10+8+11+12 \\  & =50.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 50 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Given a data set with $9$ data points and ${\sum }_{i=1}^{9}{x}_{i}=45,$ compute $\overset{―}{x}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the mean is denoted by $\overset{―}{x}$ and is given by the following formula:

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}
$$

Substituting $n=9$ and ${\sum }_{i=1}^{9}{x}_{i}=45,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot 45=5.\end{aligned}
$$
